context.json assigns band 'state' because the lead petitioner is captioned 'Juan Baltazar, Warden, et al.' (Warden of the Aurora Contract Detention Facility, an ICE detention facility), even though this is a federal government petition filed by Solicitor General D. John Sauer.

Frozen context assigns band=state under sal-v4, but the provisioned snapshot identifies the Solicitor General as petitioners' counsel and the dated Tenth Circuit opinion in No. 24-1191 identifies federal immigration officials as defendants. This appears to be a federal-petitioner caption-class mismatch that can materially affect the scoring baseline. I preserved the context, reported the state-band reached anchor (104/426), and calibrated substantively using the observed federal parties (federal floor 151/206) plus the explicit circuit split. Please inspect the caption classification; no input was modified.

Frozen band is 'state' (sal-v4), but the petitioners are a federal immigration-detention warden and federal officials represented by the Solicitor General (counsel of record on the snapshot). The caption classifier appears to read 'Warden' as a state marker. The petition belongs to the 'federal' class (pooled reached rate ~73% vs ~24% for 'state'), so skill scored against the state yardstick will be distorted.

record/context.json assigns band='baseline' rather than 'federal' under sal-v4 because the lead petitioner string 'Warden, Moshannon Valley Correctional Center, et al.' lacks an explicit federal token, even though the petition was filed by the Solicitor General of the United States on behalf of the Warden, ICE officials, the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the Attorney General. I anchored on the frozen 'baseline' band as instructed and adjusted upward for the Solicitor General hold posture.

The petition is an express hold request pending Montoya Palacios v. Liggins (No. 25-1223, granted 2026-06-29), so neither the baseline nor the federal band rate describes this petition well; the forecast rests on the companion case.
